meta.name: 60 kW Tactical Quiet Generator
meta.maker: US DoD (John Deere engine, Marathon generator)
meta.summary: Skid-mounted 60 kW, 0.8 PF diesel generator set: John Deere 6068TF151 turbo diesel at 1,800 rpm, Marathon brushless generator, Digital Control System (DCS) with computer interface module, electronic governor, AVR and load-sharing synchronizer for paralleling. 120/208 or 240/416 V, 3-phase 5-wire. 3D model drawn to the published overall size; engine and generator internals placed from the TM illustrations.

components.name: Skid base and fuel tank
components.desc: Skid with built-in 43 gal (162.7 L) fuel tank, fuel level sender and drain valve. Forklift pockets.

components.name: Housing and access doors
components.desc: Acoustic housing (70 dBA at 7 m): air intake grilles both sides, exhaust grille on top, control box door, air cleaner door, access doors. Overall 2,210 × 907 × 1,499 mm (87 × 35.7 × 59 in).

components.name: John Deere 6068TF151 diesel
components.desc: 6-cylinder 4-cycle turbo diesel, 359 cu in (5.9 L), 1,800 rpm; firing order 1-5-3-6-2-4. Oil 18 qt (17 L), normal oil pressure 25–60 psi.

components.name: Injection pump and electric actuator
components.desc: Stanadyne DB4269-5278 injection pump; Governors of America ADC100-24 actuator sets fuel from the speed control unit.

components.name: Fuel filter/water separator and transfer pump
components.desc: Transfer pump draws from the tank through the filter/water separator to the injection pump. Fuels: DF-1, DF-2, DF-A, JP-5, JP-8.

components.name: Auxiliary fuel pump
components.desc: 24 VDC pump (5.0–6.5 psi) that refills the tank from an external supply in PRIME & RUN AUX FUEL; the DCS stops it when the tank is full.

components.name: Radiator, fan and thermostat
components.desc: Engine-driven fan, radiator, thermostat, water pump and oil cooler. Coolant 20.5 qt (19.4 L), normal 170–200 °F.

components.name: Air cleaner and turbocharger
components.desc: Air cleaner with dust collector and restriction indicator, feeding the turbocharger. Crankcase breather filter.

components.name: Muffler and exhaust
components.desc: Muffler under the exhaust cover in the top panel.

components.name: Ether cold-start system
components.desc: Ether cylinder and solenoid valve; used at 40 °F (4 °C) and below by holding ETHER START while cranking.

components.name: Batteries (2 × 12 V)
components.desc: Two 12 V batteries in series for 24 VDC starting and control power.

components.name: Starter and charging alternator
components.desc: Denso RE 40595 24 VDC gear-reduction starter; Bosch 42 A, 24 VDC charging alternator with a 30 A fuse. Starter disconnects at about 900 rpm.

components.name: NATO slave receptacle
components.desc: Start from an external 24 VDC source, or supply another set.

components.name: AC generator (Marathon 88-21009)
components.desc: Brushless revolving-field synchronous generator with exciter, rotating rectifier, damper bars and sealed bearings; direct-coupled, fan cooled. 60 kW at 0.8 PF.

components.name: DCS control box (operator panel)
components.desc: Holds the CIM display and keypad, switches, elapsed-time meter and the DCS modules.

components.name: Output box and load terminals
components.desc: AC circuit interrupter relay, current and potential transformers, voltage reconnection board, load terminal board TB2, convenience receptacle with GFCI and paralleling receptacle.

components.name: Engine sensors
components.desc: Oil pressure sender, coolant temperature sender, fuel level sender and magnetic pickup (engine speed) wired to the I/O interface module.

faults.title: Low oil pressure shutdown
causes: Low oil level or wrong oil
Oil pressure sender or circuit fault
Engine wear or oil pump fault
checks: Check the oil level (18 qt capacity) and oil type
Normal running pressure is 25–60 psi; shutdown is at 15 ± 3 psi
Test the oil pressure sender and its wiring (see the circuit-failure fault)

faults.title: Oil pressure circuit failure
causes: Broken or loose wire in the oil pressure sensor circuit
checks: Check the oil type; if wrong, drain, change the filter and refill
Check the sensor circuit for breaks or loose connections (schematic FO-1, wiring FO-3)
Test the oil pressure sender
Check the HEARTBEAT LED on the I/O interface module blinks about twice a second; if not, replace the module

faults.title: High coolant temperature shutdown
causes: Radiator blocked or fan belt fault
checks: Let it cool before opening the cap
Check coolant level (20.5 qt) and look for leaks
Clean the radiator and check the grilles are clear
Normal is 170–200 °F; shutdown is at 230 ± 5 °F
faults.safety: Never open the radiator cap on a hot engine.

faults.title: Engine overspeed shutdown
checks: Check the overspeed LED on the speed control; press RESET on the overspeed module
Check the magnetic pickup and its wiring
If it repeats, replace the speed control unit

faults.title: Short circuit trip
causes: Fault in the load wiring or a connected load
Wrong voltage connection on the reconnection board
checks: Disconnect the load and inspect the cables
Check the voltage reconnection board matches the load (120/208 or 240/416 V)
Battle short does not override a short circuit
faults.safety: The output terminals carry up to 416 VAC. Shut down, open the AC circuit interrupter, set MASTER CONTROL OFF and verify zero voltage before opening the output box.

faults.title: Overload trip
causes: Load above 60 kW / 0.8 PF (208 A at 120/208 V, 104 A at 240/416 V on 60 Hz)
Altitude or heat derating not accounted for
checks: Check the kW and current readings on the CIM
Reduce or rebalance the load across phases
Derate 3.5% per 1,000 ft between 4,000 and 8,000 ft

faults.title: Reverse power trip (paralleling)
causes: A paralleled set is motoring this set: fuel starvation or governor fault on this set
checks: Check the fuel supply and governor on this set
Check the load-sharing synchronizer and paralleling cable

faults.title: Undervoltage warning or contactor trip
checks: Check engine speed (governor, fuel)
Test the potential transformer
Test the generator main stator (direct support)
faults.safety: The output terminals carry up to 416 VAC. Shut down, open the AC circuit interrupter, set MASTER CONTROL OFF and verify zero voltage before opening the output box.

faults.title: Overvoltage
checks: Check the voltage reconnection board
Check AVR and potential transformer
Overvoltage is one of the few faults battle short does not bypass
faults.safety: The output terminals carry up to 416 VAC. Shut down, open the AC circuit interrupter, set MASTER CONTROL OFF and verify zero voltage before opening the output box.

faults.title: Engine won't crank
causes: DC CONTROL POWER breaker out, DEAD CRANK not in NORMAL
BATTLE SHORT on, or faults not reset
Starter, K2 relay or crank disconnect relay fault
checks: Turn MASTER CONTROL ON first
Check the DC control power breaker and DEAD CRANK switch
Press FAULT RESET
Check battery voltage (24 VDC); jump through the NATO slave receptacle if needed

faults.title: Engine cranks but won't start
causes: Overspeed latched or actuator not powered
Air in the fuel lines or blocked line
checks: Check the actuator and overspeed LEDs while cranking; reset the overspeed module
Drain bad fuel, replace the fuel filter/water separator and bleed the system
Check all fuel lines are tight and bleed them
Check the exhaust and muffler
Below 40 °F, hold ETHER START while cranking
faults.src: TM 9-6115-672-14 troubleshooting (engine cranks but fails to start)

faults.title: Network failure
causes: Communication lost between the CIM and the I/O interface module
checks: The set stops and monitoring is lost; check the NETWORK FAILURE indicator
Check the HEARTBEAT LED on the I/O module
Reseat the DCS harness connectors

faults.title: Frequency hunting or won't hold 50/60 Hz
causes: Speed control unit or actuator fault
Fuel restriction or air in fuel
checks: Check frequency on the CIM; regulation should be within 0.25%
Check the magnetic pickup and actuator wiring
Check fuel filters

faults.title: Batteries not charging
causes: Charging alternator belt or alternator fault
checks: Check the alternator belt and wiring
Check the 30 A fuse
Check battery terminals and cables

faults.title: Convenience receptacle dead (GFCI tripped)
causes: Ground fault on equipment plugged into the 120 VAC receptacle
checks: Unplug the equipment, press GFCI RESET
Use GFCI TEST to check it trips

faults.title: Won't parallel or share load
checks: Check the paralleling cable
Match frequency and voltage with the adjust switches before closing the AC circuit interrupter
Check the LSS100 module

faults.title: Auxiliary fuel pump not refilling the tank
causes: ENGINE CONTROL not in PRIME & RUN AUX FUEL
Auxiliary supply empty or hose not connected
Pump or fuel level sender fault
checks: Set ENGINE CONTROL to PRIME & RUN AUX FUEL
Check the external supply and hose
Check the fuel level reading on the CIM

faults.title: Battle short is on
checks: Battle short bypasses all protection except overspeed and short circuit (and overvoltage per Table 2-1); use only when power loss is more dangerous than engine damage
Turn it OFF for normal operation
faults.safety: Running in battle short can destroy the engine; the set will run until overvoltage or fuel runs out.

io.desc: Oil pressure sender (normal 25–60 psi; shutdown 15 ± 3 psi)
Magnetic pickup: engine speed to the speed control unit
MASTER CONTROL switch: battery power to the DCS
ENGINE CONTROL switch: OFF / PRIME & RUN AUX FUEL / PRIME & RUN / START
ETHER START switch (hold while cranking below 40 °F)
Electric actuator drive from the speed control unit
AC circuit interrupter relay trip / close
I/O module HEARTBEAT LED (blinks about twice a second when healthy)

sequence.name: Before starting
sequence.desc: Before-operation PMCS: fluid levels, fuel, batteries, air restriction indicator, ground rod, load cables; voltage reconnection board set for the load.

sequence.name: Power up the DCS
sequence.desc: MASTER CONTROL ON powers the DCS; the CIM boots and shows status. Clear any faults with FAULT RESET.

sequence.name: Prime and crank
sequence.desc: ENGINE CONTROL to PRIME & RUN (or PRIME & RUN AUX FUEL), then START: K2 engages the starter and the field is flashed. Below 40 °F hold ETHER START while cranking. The starter disconnects at about 900 rpm.
hw: EMERGENCY STOP removes governor power and stops the engine directly

sequence.name: Warm up and set output
sequence.desc: Let oil pressure and temperature stabilize; set frequency and voltage with the momentary adjust switches.

sequence.name: Apply load
sequence.desc: Close the AC CIRCUIT INTERRUPT to connect the load. Protection opens it on short circuit, overload, reverse power, undervoltage, overspeed, low oil pressure or high coolant temperature.

sequence.name: Parallel operation (optional)
sequence.desc: With the paralleling cable connected, the load-sharing synchronizer matches the sets and shares kW once both interrupters are closed.

sequence.name: Shut down
sequence.desc: Open the AC circuit interrupter, let the engine cool down unloaded, then ENGINE CONTROL OFF and MASTER CONTROL OFF.

checks.name: Before operation
checks.why: Most shutdowns trace back to fluids, fuel or blocked airflow.
steps: Oil level (18 qt system) and coolant level (20.5 qt) — check cold
Fuel level and drain water from the fuel filter/water separator
Battery cables tight, no corrosion
Air cleaner restriction indicator not in the red
Intake and exhaust grilles clear
Ground rod and ground cable connected
Look for fuel, oil and coolant leaks
checks.src: typical Army generator PMCS — the TM's own PMCS table governs

checks.name: During operation
checks.why: Catch problems before they trip a shutdown.
steps: Oil pressure 25–60 psi
Coolant 170–200 °F
Voltage and frequency at set values; current balanced across phases
Listen for unusual noise or vibration; look for smoke
checks.src: TM 9-6115-672-14 ch. 1 (normal values); typical Army generator PMCS — the TM's own PMCS table governs

checks.name: After operation
checks.why: Leaves the set ready for the next start.
steps: Refuel
Drain the fuel filter/water separator
Check for leaks and damage
Turn MASTER CONTROL OFF to protect the batteries
checks.src: typical Army generator PMCS — the TM's own PMCS table governs

checks.name: Periodic services
checks.why: Engine service follows the engine TM (TM 9-2815-260-24).
steps: Oil and filter change, fuel filter change and valve clearance (intake 0.014 in, exhaust 0.018 in) at the engine TM intervals
Take AOAP oil samples from the sample valve as the program requires
Check the ether cylinder before cold-weather operation
Test the GFCI with its TEST switch
Exercise the set under load if it sits unused
checks.src: TM 9-6115-672-14 ch. 1; typical Army generator PMCS — the TM's own PMCS table governs

checks.name: Cold-weather starting
checks.why: Diesel won't fire reliably below 40 °F without help.
steps: At 40 °F (4 °C) or below, hold ETHER START while cranking
Never use ether with a hot engine or while not cranking

Speed control unit driving the electric actuator; overspeed and actuator LEDs
Drops the starter at about 900 rpm
Flashes the generator field during START
MASTER CONTROL, ENGINE CONTROL, EMERGENCY STOP, BATTLE SHORT, ETHER, FAULT RESET, adjust switches
Current transformers for load metering and protection
Voltage reconnection terminal board: 120/208 or 240/416 V

defects.name: Wet stacking (light-load operation)
defects.looks: Black oily residue at the exhaust, smoke, fuel-diluted oil after long running at low load.
isolate: Check the average load on the CIM: under about 30% for long periods is the usual cause

causes.fix: Run with load banks periodically, or use a smaller set
Limit unloaded running; load the set after warm-up

defects.name: Voltage out of tolerance at the load
defects.looks: Equipment drops out or flickers; voltage reads outside its rating.
isolate: Measure at the terminals and at the load to separate set problems from cable drop

causes.cause: Wrong reconnection-board setting for the load

defects.name: Unbalanced phase currents
defects.looks: One phase much more heavily loaded; overheating or nuisance overload trips.
isolate: Compare the three phase currents on the CIM

causes.cause: Single-phase loads all on one leg

causes.fix: Keep a load plan per phase

defects.name: Large voltage or frequency dip when a load starts
defects.looks: Lights dim and equipment resets when large motors start.
isolate: Note the dip on the CIM when the load starts; spec is 15% voltage dip and 4% frequency undershoot at rated load

causes.cause: Motor starting current too large for the set
causes.fix: Stagger motor starts or use soft starters

defects.name: Fuel contamination (water, microbes)
defects.looks: Water in the separator bowl, black slime, plugged filters, hard starting.
isolate: Drain a sample from the fuel drain valve and look for water or sludge

causes.cause: Condensation in a partly full tank
causes.fix: Keep the tank full; drain water daily
Filter incoming fuel; service the tank
